//: The workshop's three policies, one per hook, and the demo cast. governance.db is seeded from these, merged with gate/service/approval-guards.json, when it has no schema. Edit a row live in the database, not here: this file is read once, on first boot.

$TOOLKIT is replaced at seed time with ARCADE_TOOLKIT (default LoanDesk): one deployed server, one toolkit, every tool LoanDesk_<Tool> on the wire. Tool names are PascalCase because arcade-mcp PascalCases them unconditionally (measured on #35); a rule keyed on get_loan matches nothing, and a rule that matches nothing is indistinguishable from a rule that permits.

The placeholder is the toolkit name alone, so the separator after it is yours to choose and it means something (#89). Write $TOOLKIT.ApproveLoan in a match or anywhere naming the tool as a hook payload and an audit row do; write $TOOLKIT_ApproveLoan in a pre denial's reason, because that sentence is addressed to the model and the model can only call the name its own tool list carries. The compiler enforces the difference: a reason naming a catalogued toolkit dot-spelled does not compile.

$TOOLKIT.Decide lists an argument the tool does not take: `approval`. It is not something a caller supplies — /pre resolves the request_id against approval_requests and writes the resolved facts into that key, discarding anything the caller put there. Catalogued because a rule condition may only read a catalogued argument, and optional because a request_id naming nothing must reach pre.decide-needs-a-known-request rather than be refused as a malformed call.

subjects is the demo cast, and the first boot does NOT seed it (#33): governance.db starts with no subjects and idp.db with no users. `bun run users seed-demo` adds these four with these names, roles and clearances, under whatever addresses it is given. The @bank.example addresses are how the reset and the drift check know the demo cast: a demo row at one of them is rewritten by a reset and compared by the drift check, only where it is on disk. A demo person seeded under any other address counts as a real user.

post.redact-borrower-identifiers is conditioned on clearance: Charlie and Michael read the bank account number and tax id, Alice and Bob do not, because a control that redacts for everyone demonstrates nothing about identity. It matches every $TOOLKIT tool, not GetLoan alone (#4): ApproveLoan and DenyLoan return the same whole loan record GetLoan does, and '*' covers the next tool that returns it. SearchLoans never reads the sensitive columns, so on it the rule has nothing to remove.

policy_rules.description: Act 1. A credit analyst never sees the approval tool: it is absent from tools/list, not merely refused.
policy_rules.reason: Credit analysts do not hold approval authority; the tool is hidden from this role.

policy_rules.description: Act 2. An approval above the caller's authority is blocked, and the denial tells the model how to escalate and then retry.
policy_rules.reason: DENIED: approving {{inputs.loan_id}} for {{inputs.amount}} exceeds your approval authority of {{subject.clearance}}. To proceed, call $TOOLKIT_RequestApproval with action=approve_loan, resource_id={{inputs.loan_id}}, amount={{inputs.amount}} and justification=<why this loan should be approved>, then wait for the approval and retry $TOOLKIT_ApproveLoan with loan_id={{inputs.loan_id}} and amount={{inputs.amount}} unchanged.

output_rules.description: Act 3. Masks the borrower's bank account number and tax id for anyone whose clearance is under 250000, on every loan tool that returns the record.
output_rules.reason: Customer identifiers masked before the output reached the model.
